author: CC (captured from Akien, verbatim intent)
text: AKIEN'S METHOD, stated 2026-08-05 — the secret to making it work: 'you go back to the start, you validate every single thing along the way, all the way thru to the end point. you can either deal with necessary tangents in line, or as distinct passes. in general, things that appear either small or foundational, get done first if needed. so we're building on more solid ground. if two foundational issues, the MORE FOUNDATIONAL of them goes first.' That ordering rule is the whole reason librarian has not been reached and that is FINE — everything else is far more solid, and that is the point of the order, not a delay in it. RULED THE SAME BREATH: the one-door skill fix goes BEFORE build-order item 2 (the lines learning their own values). Why, in his words: 'because then the next one makes use of it. we test as we go for free.' A foundation laid before the next tenant arrives is exercised by that tenant at no cost; laid after, it needs its own proof and a migration. THE PATH, in his order: (1) claude [CC itself], (2) skills and workflow, (3) foundational components — ground loop, logging [flagged: 'we'll come back to that'], diagnostics, shims, bus, harbor, inspectors, probes, (4) bus services — inference domain, database domain, web server, embeddings generator, graph trees, reader, researcher mode, librarian. 'we're still on the same path.'
